# Of the Divine Chapter
<meta>catchword: Wherefore</meta>

These souls do not feel the bitterness of death: because they desire it; and with perfect hatred <note>In Catherine’s writing, "perfect hatred" is a technical term for the rejection of one's own selfish will and the physical appetites that distract from God, rather than a malicious emotion.</note> they have made war against their own bodies, whereby they have lost that tenderness that naturally exists between the soul and the body. So, having surrendered and removed natural love through hatred for the life of their body, and with love for me, such a soul desires death and then says: "Who will deliver me from my body? I desire to be dissolved from the body and be with Christ." <note>original: "esser con xpo" (esse cum Christo). A reference to Philippians 1:23.</note> And such as these also say with the same Paul: "Death is in my desire, and life is in my patience." <note>A common medieval paraphrase of Paul’s sentiments; the soul endures life only out of patient submission to God's will while yearning for the afterlife.</note>

For the soul, raised up in this perfect union, desires to see me and render me glory and praise. Therefore, returning later to the cloud of its body <note>The "cloud" represents the physical senses and the material world that obscure the direct sight of God.</note>—returning, I say, to the feeling in the body, which feeling had been withdrawn into me through the affection of love—just as I told you: that is, that all the feelings of the body were drawn away by the strength of the affection of the soul united in me more perfectly than the union between the soul and the body. 

Drawing this union to myself, then—since I told you that the body was not sufficient to bear continuous union—I depart in terms of union, but not in terms of grace nor of feeling, as I mentioned to you in the second and third states. And I always return with a greater increase of grace and with a more perfect union; wherefore I always return anew, and with more loftiness and knowledge of my truth, manifesting myself then. 

And when I depart in the manner described, so that the body may return a little to its senses, I say that because of the union I had made in the soul, and the soul in me, when the feeling of the body returns, the soul is impatient <note>In this context, "impatient" means the soul finds it difficult to endure or suffer through earthly existence.</note> in living. It sees itself removed from union with me and removed from the conversation of the immortals who render glory to me, finding itself instead in the conversation of mortals and seeing me offended so miserably. And this is the **crucified desire** <note>original: "cruciato desiderio". This is a central concept for Catherine: a longing for God so intense it feels like a crucifixion of the self, fueled by sorrow for the sins of the world.</note> that they carry: that is, to see me offended by my creatures.

Wherefore, for this reason and because of the desire to see me, their life is incomparable <note>In this context, "incomparable" suggests a state of being that transcends normal human experience or suffering.</note>; and they do not complain, because their will is no longer their own, but has been made one thing with me through love. They cannot want nor desire anything other than what I want. They delight in these things as much as they see themselves suffering; indeed, the enduring of many tribulations is a refreshment to them in the desire they have for death. Often, the desire of the will to suffer mitigates the pain they feel at being bound within the body.

These souls do not merely bear suffering with patience—as those in the third state do—but they glory in bearing many tribulations for my name. Thus, in bearing them they find delight, and in not bearing them they feel pain, fearing that I might wish to reward their good works in this life <note>A common medieval concern: that receiving earthly rewards or comfort might diminish one's "treasure in heaven."</note>, or that the sacrifice of their desires might not be pleasing to me. 

But when they endure, and when I permit many tribulations for them, they rejoice, seeing themselves clothed in the pains and shames of Christ crucified. Wherefore, if it were possible for them to possess virtue without effort, they would not want it. They would much rather delight on the cross with Christ and acquire virtue through pain than possess eternal life in any other way; for they are set on fire and drowned in the blood, where they find my blazing charity. This charity is a fire that proceeds from me and ravishes their heart and their mind, igniting the sacrifice of their desires. Thus the eye of the intellect raises itself, contemplating my deity, where...

**Law**. <note>original: "Io nō sō uēuto a dissoluere la leze: ma ad īpirla" — I have not come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it (Matthew 5:17).</note> **I have not come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it**, as if his life said to them: the law is now imperfect, but with my blood alone I will make it perfect; and so I will refill it with that which it now lacks, taking away the fear of punishment and founding it in love and in holy fear. Wherefore, such as these marvel and fall into grumbling, seeing many <term>simple: "grossi," people without formal education</term> and <term>unlearned: "idioti," from the Latin "idiota," meaning a layperson or someone without academic degrees</term> folks in the knowledge of Holy Scripture; and nevertheless, they are so illuminated in knowing the truth as if they had studied it for a long time. This is no wonder at all, because they have studied the principal cause of the light, from which knowledge comes. But because those proud ones have lost the light, they do not see nor recognize my goodness in the light of grace poured out upon my servants. Wherefore I tell you, that it is much better to go for counsel regarding the salvation of the soul to a humble person with a holy and upright conscience than to a proud, literate man studying much <note>original: "scientia" — referring here to academic theology or human learning</note> science; for that man offers nothing except what he has within himself; wherefore, through his dark life, he will often offer the light of Holy Scripture in darkness. And therefore the ignorant, proud scholars blind themselves in the light: because pride and the cloud of self-love have obscured and taken away this light; and therefore they understand Scripture more literally than with true understanding. Hence, for this reason, they taste only the letter, turning over many books, and they do not taste the <term>marrow: "medulla," the spiritual essence or deepest meaning</term> of the Scripture, because they have removed the light with which Scripture is formed and declared. 

Wherefore such people marvel and fall into grumbling, seeing many <term>simple and unlearned: "grossi & idioti," meaning those without formal academic or theological training</term> who are so knowledgeable in Holy Scripture, and who are nonetheless so illuminated in knowing the truth as if they had studied it for a long time. This is no marvel at all, because they have studied the principal cause of the light from which science comes. 

But because those proud ones have lost the light, they do not see nor recognize my goodness in the light of grace poured upon my servants. Wherefore I tell you: it is much better to go for counsel regarding the **salvation of the soul** to a humble person with a holy and upright conscience than to a proud, lettered man studying in much science; for that man offers only what he has within himself. Often, because of his darkened life, he will offer the light of Holy Scripture in darkness. The opposite is found in my servants: because the light that they have in them, they offer with **hunger**:

### How there are five kinds of tears. Chapter 88.

Most beloved: and dearest daughter: you ask me wanting to know the reasons for tears and their fruits: and I have not despised your desire. But first I will speak of the tears of the wicked men of the world: these are tears of damnation. <header>Providence LXXXIX</header>

the fountain of the heart. But because the soul has not yet reached great perfection: it often sheds sensory tears: and if you ask me why, I respond to you: it is because of the root of self-love. It is no longer a sensory <term>self-love: "amore proprio," a focus on one's own desires rather than God's will</term>, for I have already removed that through the method I mentioned, but it is a spiritual love. Hence, when the soul is deprived of that thing which it loves—that is, of consolation both internal and external (internal consolation that it had drawn from me, and external consolation it had through other people)—and when temptations or the persecutions of men arise, the heart feels pain. From this, it draws a true knowledge of my goodness with a fire of love, and begins to unite and conform its will with mine. Thus, it begins to feel both joy and compassion. # Of the Divine Chapter
<meta>catchword: me never</meta>

...to know their evils through their own punishment <note>original: "propria pena"</note>: which follows them after the fault. This is a general beginning kindly given by me to the frail ones: who, like ignorant people, drown down in the river: shunning the doctrine of my life. 

But there are many who recognize their evils without servile fear <term>servile fear: a state where one avoids sin only out of fear of punishment or hell, rather than out of love for God</term>: that is, [fear] of their own punishment: and some go immediately with a great hatred of themselves: through which hatred they consider themselves worthy of the punishment. And some, with a good simplicity, give themselves to fleeing to me, their creator: grieving for the offense they have done to me. And I want that person to be proven to reach the perfect state: who goes with very great hatred: although, by exercising themselves, both the one and the other reach it: but this one reaches it first. One must therefore take care not to remain in servile fear: and the other in their lukewarmness: that is, that in that simplicity, by not exercising it, they do not grow lukewarm within: so that this is a common cry. 

The third and the fourth [states] are those of people who, lifted from fear, have reached love: and hope: tasting my divine mercy: receiving many gifts: and consolations from me: for which the eye, which satisfies the feeling of the heart, weeps. But because it is still imperfect: and mixed with spiritual sensory weeping <note>Tears that still stem from the soul's own feelings and desires for comfort rather than pure love</note>: as was said: one reaches it by exercising somewhat in virtue: where the soul, having grown in desire, joins herself: and conforms herself to my will: so much so that she cannot will: nor desire except that which I want: clothed in the charity of the neighbor <note>original: "charita del prossimo"</note>: wherefore she draws a weeping of love within herself from the sorrow of the offense against me: and the harm to the neighbor. 

This is joined with the fifth: and final perfection: where she is joined [to me] in life: and where the fire of holy desire has grown: from which desire the devil flees: and cannot strike the soul: neither by injury that might be done to her: because she has been made patient in the charity of the neighbor: nor by spiritual: or temporal consolation: because through hatred <note>In this context, a holy "hatred" or rejection of the selfish ego and sin</note>: and true humility she despises it. And it is very true: that the devil, for his part, never sleeps...

# Providence XC
### Dialogue of St. Catherine M ii

...me never: but it teaches its negligent ones: that in the time of gain you were sleeping. But his <note>the devil's</note> watchfulness cannot harm these people: because he cannot endure the heat of their charity: nor the fragrance of the union: which has made me a peaceful sea: where the soul cannot be deceived: while it remains joined in me: so that he flees like the fly does from the pot that boils on the fire for fear: that it has of the fire. But if it were lukewarm: it would not fear but would go inside: although many times it dies there, finding it hotter: than it imagined. 

Thus it happens to the soul: before it comes to the perfect state: wherefore the devil, because it seems lukewarm to him: enters within it with many diverse temptations. But if there is a point of self-knowledge <note>original: "cognoscimento"</note>: and of heat <note>original: "colore", likely a transcription of "calore" (heat), continuing the metaphor of the boiling pot</note>: and displeasure for the fault: it resists, binding the will: so that it does not consent, with the bond of the hatred of sin: and of the love of virtue. Every soul rejoices: that feels many troubles: because that is the way to reach this sweet: & glorious state. 

Because I already told you: that through the knowledge: & hatred of yourselves: and through the knowledge of my goodness: you come to perfection: wherefore there is no time: that the soul knows so well: if I am in it: as in the time of many battles. In what way? I tell it to you: it knows well: seeing itself in battles: that it cannot free itself: nor resist by its own will: so as not to have those battles: & then it can know itself to be nothing <term>nothingness: Catherine's central theological concept that the human being has no existence of their own, but exists only through God's continuous creation</term>: because if it were anything by itself: it would remove those battles: that it does not want. 

So therefore in this way it humbles itself with true self-knowledge: and with the light of the most holy faith it runs to me, Eternal God: through which goodness it finds itself with its good: and holy will: which does not consent at the time of the many battles to follow the miseries in which it feels now...

### ¶ How those who desire the tears of the eyes and cannot have them, have the tears of fire; and for what reason God withdraws physical tears. Chapter 91.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'D' containing a portrait of a religious figure, possibly a saint or nun, wearing a habit and cowl.</image-desc>I have spoken to you of perfect and imperfect tears, and how they all come from the heart. From this vessel every tear emerges, for whatever reason it may be, and so they can all be called "tears of the heart." The only difference lies in ordered and disordered love; in perfect and imperfect love, as was said above. It remains now for me to speak, to satisfy your desire, of some who would wish for the perfection of tears and do not seem able to have them. Is there then another way to weep? Yes indeed: there is a weeping of fire, that is, of a true and holy desire, which consumes itself through the affection of love, and would wish to dissolve its life in weeping for hatred of itself and for the salvation of souls <note>Original: *salute d laie* (salute de l'anime)</note>—yet it seems it cannot. I say, then, that these have the "tears of fire," in which the Holy Spirit <note>Original: *spō sctō* (Spiritu Sancto)</note> weeps before me for them and for their neighbor <note>Original: *pxio* (prossimo)</note>. That is to say, my divine charity sets the soul ablaze with its flame, so that she offers anxious desires before me without the tears of the eyes. I say that these are tears of fire; and in this way it was said that the Holy Spirit wept. Wherefore these, not being able to do so with tears, offer the desires of the will which has been seized for love of me. For sometimes I permit not giving the soul physical tears, in order to keep it continually before me, humbled, and in constant prayer <note>original: *ɔtiua or̃one* (continua oratione)</note> and a desire to "taste" me. So, for the sake of increase and not for decrease, I withdraw the gift of actual tears of the eye, but I give the soul mental ones alone, coming from the heart and filled with the fire of my divine **charity** <term>charity: from the Latin *caritas*, meaning a selfless, sacrificial love for God and neighbor</term>.

This is the variety and the explanation of the states of the aforementioned tears, declared by me, Eternal Life, to you, my sweetest daughter. Drown yourself, then, in the blood of Christ crucified, the immaculate lamb, my only-begotten Son, with humble suffering <note>original: *humile cruciato*</note>, growing in continual virtue, so that the fire of my divine charity may be nourished within you.

### [The quanti]tity of tears: and that God wishes to be served by something infinite. Chapter 92.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'Q' featuring floral and vine motifs within a square border.</image-desc>

These five aforementioned states are like five principal channels: four of which provide an abundance of an infinite variety of tears; all of these give life if they are practiced in virtue, as has been said. And when I say "infinite," I do not mean that in this life you are infinite in weeping; rather, I call them "infinite" because of the infinite desire of the soul. Now I have told you how tears proceed from the heart, and how the heart offers them to the eye, having gathered them in burning desire—much like green wood <note>original: *legno uerde*</note> placed in the fire, which, because of the heat, "weeps" water. It does this because it is green; for if it were dry, it would not weep. So does the heart made green again by the renewal of **grace** <term>grace: the divine influence which operates in humans to regenerate and sanctify</term>; it draws out the dryness of its own selfish humors <note>original: *humore pprio*; referring to the medieval medical belief that bodily fluids influenced spiritual disposition</note> (which wither the soul) through burning desire.

And because desire never ends, it is not completed in this life; instead, the more the soul loves, the less it seems to love, and thus it exercises holy desire founded in **charity** <term>charity: in this context, the highest form of love, signifying a selfless devotion to God and others</term>, with which desire the eye weeps. But once the soul is separated from the body and joined to me, its final end, it does not abandon its desire; it continues to desire me and the charity of its neighbor. This is because charity has entered within as a gift, carrying with it the fruit of all other virtues. It is true, however, that the suffering and pain end, as I told you; for if the soul desires me, it truly possesses me without any fear of losing what it has desired for so long.

And in this state, hunger is nourished; but in having hunger, they are satisfied, and in being satisfied, they have hunger <note>This paradox describes the experience of Heaven: a state of perfect fulfillment that never becomes boring, where one is always "full" yet always "hungry" for more of God's goodness</note>. Yet the weariness of being full is far removed, as is the pain of hunger, because there they lack no perfection. So you see, your desire is infinite; otherwise, no virtue would have any value for life if I were served by you only with something finite. Wherefore, because I am an infinite God, I desire nothing from you but affection and the desire

### ¶ Of the fruit of the tears of worldly men. Chap. xciii.

[It] is a tree that produces nothing but fruits of death: rotten flowers: stained leaves: its branches are bent down even to the earth, beaten by diverse winds. This is the tree of the **soul** <note>original: *lania* (l'anima)</note>; and because you are all **trees of love** <term>arbore damore: a recurring metaphor in Catherine’s writing where the soul is seen as a tree that must be planted in the soil of God's love</term>, you cannot live without love, because you were made by me for love. Wherefore the soul that lives virtuously places the root of its tree in the valley of true **humility** <term>humilita: the fundamental virtue in Catherine’s theology, contrasted with the "mountain" of pride</term>; but these who live miserably have placed it on the mountain of **pride** <term>supbia (superbia): considered the root of all other sins</term>. Because it is poorly planted, it does not produce fruits of life, but of death.

And the fruits are their actions, which are all poisoned by many and diverse sins; and if they perform any fruit of good action, because the root is corrupt everything comes out spoiled. That is to say: the soul that is in **mortal sin** <term>peccato mortale: a grave sin that severs the soul's relationship with God's grace</term>, no good action that it performs is of value for eternal life, because they are not done in **grace** <term>gratia: the divine life of God within the soul</term>. Although one must not abandon good action, because every good is rewarded and every fault is punished.

The good, therefore, that has been done outside of grace is not sufficient, nor does it avail for eternal life, as I have said. But the divine goodness is a **justice** <note>original: *iustitia*</note> that gives imperfect reward, just as imperfect service is given to me. Whence sometimes it is rewarded in temporal things; sometimes I lend them time—as I narrated to you in another place regarding this matter—giving them space so that they may correct themselves.

This also I will sometimes do for them: that is, I will give them the life of grace through some means of my servants, who are pleasing and acceptable to me; just as I did for the glorious **Apostle Paul** <note>original: *apostolo paulo*</note> who, through the prayer of **Saint Stephen** <note>original: *sancto stephano*; referring to the tradition that Stephen's prayer while being stoned led to Paul's later conversion</note>, rose from his infidelity and from the persecutions that he carried out against the Christians. So you see well that in whatever state a person may be, they must never cease from doing good.

I was telling you that the flowers of this tree were rotten, and such is the truth. The flowers are the stinking thoughts of the heart, which are displeasing to me, and are hatred and displeasure...

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'Q' featuring floral motifs within a square frame.</image-desc>

**These** individuals are beaten by many winds: either the wind of **prosperity** <note>original: *prosperita*</note>, or the wind of **adversity** <note>original: *aduerſita*</note>, or of **fear** <note>original: *timore*</note>, or of **conscience** <note>original: *coscientia*</note>: which are four winds. This wind of prosperity is corrupt in itself: because the principal root of the tree is corrupt: wherefore everything is corrupted: for I, who send and give everything that has being, am supremely good: and therefore, everything that this wind carries is [intrinsically] good <note>God explains that while the blessings of prosperity are good because they come from Him, the sinner’s corrupt heart turns them into a source of pride.</note>. After this comes a wind of **servile fear** <term>timore seruile: a "slavish" fear of punishment or loss, rather than a "filial" fear born of love for God.</term>, in which his own shadow makes him afraid: fearing to lose the thing that he loves: wherefore he fears losing his very life: or that of his children: or of other creatures: or he fears losing his status: or others for self-love: or honor: or wealth. This fear does not let him possess his delight in peace: and this is because he does not possess it in an orderly way according to my will: and therefore servile and fearful dread follows him. And he is made miserable by **sin** <note>original: *pctō* (peccato)</note>: and such a thing can be considered as nothing, for it comes through sin, and sin is nothingness; therefore he has come to nothing. While the wind of fear has struck him, he also reaches that of tribulation and of adversity, which he feared, and it deprives him of that which he had: and this

And through the delight and consolation it finds in Me, it begins to love very sweetly, feeling the sweetness of My consolation, or that which comes from other creatures through Me.

By exercising this love in the house of its soul—which entered in after fear had purified it—it begins to receive the fruits of My divine goodness. Thus it holds the house of its soul; and once love has entered to take possession, it begins to taste, receiving many varied and diverse fruits of consolation.

Persevering to the end, it receives the fruit of "setting the table." This means that after the soul has passed from fear to the love of virtues, it places itself at its table, joined to the **third state of tears** <note>St. Catherine describes five stages of "tears" or spiritual development; the third stage represents the transition from a servant's fear to a friend's love</note>. It places itself, I say, at the table of the **most holy cross** <note>original: *sctissima croce*</note> in its heart and in its soul. Once it has set this table, it finds there the food of the sweet and loving **Word** <note>original: *uerbo*; the Logos or Christ</note>, who demonstrates My honor as Father and your salvation. For this salvation, the body of My **only-begotten Son** <note>original: *unigenito mio figliolo*</note> was opened, giving Himself to you as food. Then the soul begins to eat of My honor and the salvation of souls, filled with hatred and displeasure for **sin** <note>original: *pctõ / peccato*</note>.

What fruit does the soul receive in this **third state**? I tell you: it receives a strength founded in a holy hatred of its own **sensuality** <note>original: *ppa tẽsualita*; the ego-driven or physical desires that compete with the spirit</note>, along with the pleasant fruit of your **humility** <note>original: *hūilita*</note> and a **patience** <note>original: *patiẽtia*</note> that removes all offense. This patience deprives the soul of every pain, because the "knife of hatred" <note>A common Catherinian metaphor for the ascetic practice of "killing" one's selfish will</note> kills the soul's own **will** <note>original: *uolūta*</note>, which is where every fault resides. For only the **sensory will** <note>original: *uolunta sensitiua*; the part of the will that reacts to pleasure and pain</note> is scandalized by injuries, or by persecutions in temporal and spiritual consolations—as I told you above—and thus it falls into impatience.

But because the will is dead through tearful and sweet desire, it begins to taste the fruit of the "tear of sweet patience." Oh, fruit of great sweetness, how sweet you are to those who taste you! And how...

<summary>This page describes the soul's progression from a state of fear to one of love, where the soul "furnishes" itself with virtue and "eats" at the table of the Cross. It emphasizes that by "killing" the selfish will through holy hatred of one's own sensuality, the soul gains a patience that makes it immune to the pain of earthly persecution.</summary>

# From the Divine Chapter
<meta>catchword: from the</meta>

...you are pleasing to Me: you who, while remaining in bitterness, taste sweetness; in times of injury, you receive peace. In the time when you are on a tempestuous sea, and when perilous winds and great waves beat against the **little ship of the soul** <note>original: *nauicella de laia*; a common medieval metaphor for the individual's spiritual journey</note>, you remain peaceful and tranquil, without any harm, having sheltered that little ship within My sweet eternal will. From this will, the soul has received the garment of true and most ardent **charity** <note>original: *charita*; divine love as opposed to mere human affection</note>, so that the waters of the world cannot enter into it. 

O most beloved daughter, this royal patience is placed upon the rock of fortitude. She conquers and is never conquered. She is not alone, but is accompanied by **perseverance**. She is the marrow of charity; she is the one who makes visible the garment of that charity. She is the wedding garment and the wheel of perfection. She also reveals herself the moment she experiences the opposite, which is impatience. 

All the virtues can, at times, be hidden, appearing to be perfect when they are actually imperfect. However, these cannot be hidden; for if that sweet patience—the marrow of charity—is within the soul, she demonstrates that all the virtues are alive and perfect. But if patience is not manifest, it is clear that all the virtues are imperfect and have not yet reached the table of the **most holy cross** <note>original: *sanctissima croce*</note>. It is there that patience was conceived, in the knowledge of oneself and in the knowledge of My goodness within the soul; she is given birth by **holy hatred** <note>original: *lodio sctō*; a technical term in Catherine's spirituality for the rejection of one's own selfish will and ego</note> and anointed with true humility. 

To this patience, the food of My honor and the salvation of the soul is never denied. Indeed, she is the one who eats of it continually, and thus she is truth. Look, My dearest daughter, at the sweet and glorious martyrs: by enduring, they ate the food of souls. Their death gave life; they raised the dead and cast out the darkness of mortal sins. The world with all its greatness, and lords with all their power, could not defend themselves against them, because of the power of this queen, sweet patience. This virtue is like a lamp upon a candlestick; this is the glorious fruit that...

It highlights the martyrs as the supreme examples of those who used patience to overcome worldly power and win souls.</summary>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'D' containing a portrait of a person, likely a saint or the author, in profile.</image-desc> I have spoken to you of the fruit of the third tears; let us follow now with the fourth and final state of **unitive tears** <note>original: *lachryma unitiua*; the highest stage of mystical prayer where the soul feels perfectly joined to God</note>. However, the soul has grown so much upon reaching the fourth stage that it no longer merely bears persecutions with patience, as I told you before, but it desires them with joy. This soul, then, receives a fire of mental peace and a union forged through the feeling of My sweet divine mercy. There, it tastes milk, just as a pacified child rests at its mother’s breast; by holding the mother’s breast in its mouth, the child draws the milk to itself through the medium of the flesh. So too the soul, having reached this final state, rests at the breast of My divine charity and holds in the mouth of **holy desire** <note>original: *sancto desiderio*</note> the flesh of Christ crucified—that is, by following His footsteps and His doctrine. # Chapter IV: On the Divine [Truth]

...to bear and reach proven virtues: so that she then rests on the breast of **Christ crucified** <note>original: *xp̃o crucifixo*</note>, who is Truth itself. Thus, she drew to herself the milk of virtue, in which virtue she possessed the life of grace, tasting within herself My divine mercy, which gave sweetness to the virtues. And such is the truth: for in themselves, the virtues were not sweet; but they are made sweet because they were made and joined in Me, divine love. This means that the soul had no regard for her own utility, nor for anything else but My honor and the salvation of souls.

Now look, sweet daughter, how sweet and glorious is this state, in which the soul has achieved such union at the breast of **charity** <note>original: *charita*; divine, selfless love</note> that the mouth is not found without the breast, nor the breast without the milk. And so this soul is not found without Christ crucified, nor without Me, the Eternal Father, whom she finds by tasting the supreme eternal deity. 

Oh, if only one could see how the powers of that soul are filled! The memory fills with a continuous remembrance of Me, drawn to herself by the love of My benefits—not just the act of the benefits, but the affection of My charity with which I gave them to her. And singularly, she remembers the benefit of **creation** <note>original: *creatiōe*</note>, seeing herself created in My image and likeness. In this benefit, within the first state, she recognized the pain that followed her ingratitude; and then she rose from those miseries through the benefit of the **blood of Christ** <note>original: *sangue di christo*</note>, where I recreated her in grace, washing the face of your souls from the leprosy of sin. 

There, the soul finds a sweetness in the second state, tasting the sweetness of love and the displeasure for her fault. In this, she sees that her sin was so displeasing to Me that I punished it upon the body of My only-begotten Son. After this, she has found the coming of the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: *spirito sancto*</note>, who clarified and clarifies the soul regarding the **truth** <note>original: *uerita*</note>. When does the soul receive this light? She receives it after she has known, through the first and second states, My benefit within herself. Then she receives perfect light, knowing the truth of Me, the Eternal Father.

# Concerning the Divine Chapter

...there remain for the darkness two lights derived from this light which are necessary for you to possess, and also a third. The first is that you all should be enlightened to recognize the transitory things of the world, which all pass away like the wind. But you cannot recognize them well if you do not first recognize your own fragility, and how much it is inclined toward a <term>perverse law<note>original: "lege puerfa"; a reference to the "law of the members" or the inclination toward sin (concupiscence) described by St. Paul in the New Testament</note></term> which is bound within your members to rebel against me, your Creator. Not that anyone can be forced by this law to commit even the smallest sin if they do not wish to; rather, it fights against the spirit. I did not give this law so that my creature, who possesses reason, should be defeated, but so that it might increase and prove the virtue in the soul, because virtue is not proven except by its contrary. Therefore, <term>sensuality<note>original: "sensualita"; refers to the lower, physical nature and desires of the human being</note></term> is contrary to the spirit, and through this sensuality, the soul proves the love it has for me, its Creator. When does it prove it? When, with hatred and displeasure, it rises up against [sensuality]. I also gave this law to preserve the soul in your humility.

Hence, it is clear that in creating the soul in my image and likeness, and placing it in such dignity and beauty, I accompanied it with the vilest thing there is: giving it the perverse law—that is, binding it to a body formed from the vilest parts of the earth—so that seeing its own beauty, it would not lift its head in pride against me. Therefore, the fragile body, which acts as this <note>original: "fūe"; literally "rope" or "tether"</note> tether, is the cause of making the soul humble; it has no reason for pride, but rather for true and perfect humility. So you see, this law does not compel one toward any fault of sin by any of its attacks, but it is the means of making you know yourselves and the lack of stability in the world.

This, therefore, the eye of the intellect must see with the light of the most holy faith, which I told you was the pupil of the eye. This is that necessary light which is generally needed by every creature that possesses reason within itself.

<vocab>light, fragility, creator, spirit, virtue, sensuality, humility, soul, body, pride, faith, intellect</vocab>

<summary>God explains that the "perverse law" of physical desire was given not to force humans into sin, but to foster humility and provide a "contrary" through which virtue and love for God can be proven. This awareness of one's own fragility is the first necessary light of the intellect, guided by faith.</summary>

<keywords>perverse law, humility, fragility of the body, virtue through conflict, sensuality vs spirit, light of faith, self-knowledge, Catherine of Siena</keywords>

# From the Divine Chapter
<meta>catchword: to have:</meta>

one must grow either in the common light which they have acquired through my **grace**, or they must diligently strive to go toward the second perfect light; and from the imperfect, reach the perfect: because one must walk toward perfection with light. In this second perfect light, there are two types of perfect people—perfect, I say, in that they have risen above the common way of living in the world—and in this perfection there are two states. 

The first is composed of those who perfectly give themselves over to chastising their bodies, performing harsh and very great <term>penance<note>original: "penitētia"; voluntary physical suffering or discipline intended as an expression of repentance</note></term>. And so that their sensuality does not rebel against reason, they have all placed their desire more in **mortifying the body** than in killing their own **will**: as I told you in another place. These people feed themselves at the table of penance: and they are good and perfect, provided that this penance is founded in me with the light of <term>discretion<note>original: "discretione"; the spiritual gift of discernment that allows a person to balance practices like fasting with the actual needs of the soul and the demands of love</note></term>: that is, with a true <term>knowledge<note>original: "cognoscimēto"; a central theme for Catherine, referring to the "cell of self-knowledge" where one discovers both their own nothingness and God's infinite love</note></term> of themselves and of me, and with great **humility**, all conformed and joined to my will and not to the will of men. 

But if they were not so—that is, if they were not clothed in my will with true humility—they would often offend their own perfection by making themselves judges of those who do not walk by that same path they walk. Do you not know what would happen to such people? It is because they have placed more study and desire in **mortifying the body** than in killing their own **will**. These sorts of people always want to choose times, and places, and consolations of the mind according to their own way, and also the tribulations of the world and the battles of the devil, just as I told you regarding the second imperfect state. 

These, I say, are deceived by themselves, being deceived by their own will, which I called **spiritual self-will**. They say to themselves: "I would like this consolation, and I would not want these battles and troubles from the devil; and I do not say this for my own sake, but to please God more, and to have Him more through grace in my soul: because it seems better to me **to have**...

<summary>God explains that some seekers focus too much on physical penance (fasting and hardship) rather than surrendering their internal will. This "spiritual self-will" leads them to judge others and demand specific spiritual experiences rather than accepting what God provides.</summary>

# Providence C <note>original: "Prouidentia C"; likely an abbreviation for a chapter or section concerning Divine Providence</note>

gate: and through it you must enter into me, the **peaceful sea**. <note>The "peaceful sea" is one of Catherine’s most famous metaphors for the infinite and tranquil nature of God.</note> I say, then, that this is the perfection of the soul: that when the soul has arrived at tasting this light—which she saw and knew so sweetly—and has then tasted it, she then runs like one enamored and anxious with love to the table of **holy desire**. <term>Holy desire: a central concept for Catherine, representing a soul's burning longing for God and the salvation of others.</term> And she does not see herself—that is, she does not seek her own consolation, neither spiritual nor temporal—but like a person who is entirely within this light and knowledge, she has denied her own will and does not avoid any labor, from whichever side it comes. 

Even while sustaining pain, enduring the reproach and troubles of the devil and the murmuring of men, she eats at the table of the **most holy cross** the food of the honor of Me, the eternal God, and of the salvation of souls. She seeks no reward, neither from me nor from creatures, because she is stripped of **mercenary love**—that is, of loving me for her own sake—and is clothed in the perfect light, loving me sincerely and without any other regard than the glory and praise of my name. She does not serve me for her own delight, nor her neighbor for her own utility, but for pure love. 

These souls have lost themselves; they have stripped themselves of the **old man** <note>original: "lhomo uechio"; a biblical reference to the sinful, fallen nature of humanity (Colossians 3:9)</note> of their own sensuality and clothed themselves in the **new man** of Christ, sweet Jesus my Truth, following Him manfully. And though they have indeed mortified the body, they do not do so as their principal focus, but as an **instrument**; for the body helps in killing one's own will, just as I told you when I explained that word: that I wanted "few words and many deeds" <note>This refers to an earlier passage in the Dialogue where God emphasizes that external rituals and words matter less than the internal "deed" of love and the sacrifice of the will.</note>, and so you must do. For the principal focus must be on killing the will, so that it seeks and wants nothing else than to follow my sweet Truth, **Christ crucified**.

# Of the Divine Chapter <note>original: "De la diuina Capitolo"</note>

...seeking the honor and the glory of my name and the **salvation of souls**. <term>Salvation of souls: "salute de l'anime," a core theme in Catherine's writing, referring to the spiritual rescue and well-being of others.</term> These who are in this **sweet light** <note>original: "dolce lūe"</note> do so; and therefore they remain always in peace and in quiet. They have no stumbling blocks that cause them scandal, because they have taken away that thing which causes them scandal: that is, their **own will**. <term>Own will: "ppria uolūta," the selfish desires that Catherine identifies as the root of all sin and suffering.</term> And all the persecutions that the world can give, and the devil, run beneath their feet as they stay within the water of many tribulations and temptations; and it does not harm them because they stay attached to the vine of burning desire.

These enjoy every thing and are not made judges of my servants, nor of any creature who possesses reason; but they enjoy every state and every manner that they see, saying: "Grace be to you, **Eternal Father** <note>original: "padre eterno"</note>, for in your house you have **many mansions**." <note>A reference to John 14:2, emphasizing that there are many different paths to God.</note> And they enjoy the diverse ways they see even more than if they saw everyone walking along a single path, because they see more clearly the greatness of my goodness; thus from everything they enjoy and draw out the scent of the rose. 

And not only from the good, but even from that thing which they see is expressly sin, they do not take judgment, but rather a wholesome and true **compassion**, praying to me for those sinners; and with **perfect humility** <note>original: "humilita perfecta"</note> they say: "Today it happens to you, and tomorrow to me, were it not for the divine grace that preserves me." 

O dearest daughter, fall in love with this sweet and excellent state, and look at these souls, how they run in this glorious light and their excellence; for they have holy minds and eat at the table of **holy desire** <note>original: "sancto d'siderio"</note> and with the light they have come to nourish themselves with the food of souls for the honor of me, the Eternal Father, clothed in the garment of the **sweet lamb** <note>original: "dolce agnello"</note>, my only-begotten son: that is, his doctrine with burning **charity**. <term>Charity: "charita," signifying the highest form of love—selfless, divine love for God and neighbor.</term> These do not lose time giving false judgments, neither toward my servants nor toward those of the world; they are not scandalized by any murmuring, neither for themselves nor for others. That is, toward themselves they are content

In fact, if you remember well, you returned to the consciousness of your body as my Truth said to you: "Do you wish to reach **perfect purity**, and to be freed from scandals, so that your mind will not be scandalized by anything? Now, see to it that you always join yourself to me through the affection of love. For I am the supreme and eternal purity; I am that **fire** which purifies the soul. The closer a soul draws to me, the purer it becomes; and the further it moves away, the more unclean it is." This is why the men of the world fall into such **wickedness**: because they are separated from me. But the soul that joins itself to me without any intermediary <note>original: "senza mezo," implying a direct, unmediated mystical union.</note> participates in my purity.

One other thing you must do to reach this union and purity: you must never judge the **will of man** in anything you might see done or said by any creature, whether it is directed toward you or toward others. Instead, consider only my **will** in them and in yourself. And if you should see sin...

Therefore, it is necessary for you, if you wish to come to the purity you ask of me, to do these three principal things: namely, to join yourself to me through the affection of love, bearing in your memory the benefits received from me; to see with the eye of the intellect the affection of my **charity** <term>Charity: "charità," the supreme virtue of selfless, divine love.</term>, for I love you inestimably; and in the will of man, to judge my will and not their ill-will, for I am the judge of it, and not you. ### ¶ In what way they receive the earnest money of eternal life, those who remain in the aforesaid perfection. Chapter 101.

And because I told you that they receive the **earnest money** of eternal life, I say that they receive the earnest, but not as full payment. Instead, they wait to receive it in me, in the **enduring life**, where there is life without death, satiety without disgust, and hunger without the pain of longing. I say that the pain of hunger is removed because they have what they desire, and the disgust of satiety is removed because I am the **food of life** without any defect. 

Therefore, I will that in this life they receive the earnest money and taste it in this way: that is, the soul <note>original: "laia," likely "l'anima" (the soul) or continuing the "arra" (earnest) metaphor.</note> begins to be hungry for the honor of me, Eternal God, and for the food of the soul’s salvation. And as she has hunger, so she feeds upon it; that is, the soul nourishes herself on the **charity of her neighbor**, for whom she has hunger and desire. This is a food that, while nourishing her, never satiates her, because it is insatiable, and so there remains a continual hunger. 

And just as the earnest money is a beginning of security given to a person, by which they expect to receive the payment—not that the earnest is perfect in itself, but it provides faith and certainty of reaching the completion and receiving one's payment—so this soul, in love and clothed in the doctrine of my Truth, has received the earnest money in this life through my charity and that of her neighbor in herself...

### ¶ In what way one must rebuke the neighbor, so that the person does not fall into false judgment. Chapter 102.

Dearest daughter: pay close attention now to what I will tell you. In order that you may be better informed about what you asked me, I have told you of the **common light**, which all of you should have in whatever state you are: that is, I speak of those who remain in **common charity**. And I have told you of those who are in the **perfect light**, which light I distinguished for you in two ways: that is, those who were lifted from the world and strove to **mortify their bodies**; and others who completely killed their **own will**. And these, I said, were those perfect ones who nourish themselves at the table of the **holy desire**.

### ¶ A summary repetition of the aforementioned things with an addition concerning the correction of one's neighbor. Chapter 105.

Now I have told you, dearest daughter, satisfying your desire to have me explain what you asked of me: namely, in what way you ought to **reprove your neighbor** <note>original: "reprehēdere el pximo tuo" — the act of fraternal correction or pointing out a neighbor's fault</note>. This is so that you are not deceived by the devil, nor by your own low vision. I have told you that you should reprove in general, and not in particular, unless you have received an express revelation from me. Instead, with humility and in the manner I have described, you should "reprove yourself in them" <note>This refers to the practice of seeing one's own potential for sin when observing the faults of others, thereby maintaining humility</note>. I have also told you, and I say it again, that in no way in the world is it permitted for you to **judge** any creature—neither in general nor in particular—nor to judge the minds of my servants, whether you find them well-disposed or not.

And I have told you the reason why you cannot judge: for by judging, you would remain deceived in your own judgment. Instead, you and others must have compassion, and leave the judgment to me. I have also told you the doctrine and the principal foundation that you should give to those who might come to you for counsel, and who wish to leave the darkness of **mortal sin** and follow the way of truth. That is, you should give them as a starting principle and foundation the affection and the love of **virtue** through the knowledge of themselves and of my goodness within them. Let them kill and drown their own will so that nothing within them rebels against me. And let them use **penance** as an instrument, and not as the principal focus—as has been said—and not equally for everyone, but according to...

Suppose that the whole world were to communicate in the light and the heat of this sun; even so, this true sun, my only-begotten Son, is not detached from me alone, the Eternal Father, even though he is administered to everyone who wishes to receive him within the <term>mystical body<gloss>original: "corpo mistico." The concept of the Church as a collective spiritual body with Christ as the head.</gloss></term> of the holy church. But he remains whole, and you have him as whole God and whole man; just as I gave you the example of the light: that is, if the whole world went for that light, all would have it, and yet it would remain whole.

# Providence 111
### Dialogue of St. Catherine, Part 4

Dearest daughter: open well the eye of your <term>intellect<gloss>original: "intellecto." In medieval theology, the intellect is the faculty of the soul that perceives spiritual truths beyond the physical senses.</gloss></term> to gaze upon the abyss of my charity: for there is no creature who possesses reason whose heart should not break with the affection of love when looking, among the other benefits you have received from me, upon the benefit you receive in this <term>sacrament<gloss>The Eucharist or Holy Communion, which Catholics believe becomes the literal body and blood of Christ.</gloss></term>. 

And with what eye, dearest daughter, should you and others see and regard this mystery? And how should you touch it? Not only with the touch and sight of the body, because all the physical senses fail here. You see that the eye perceives nothing other than the whiteness of that bread; the hand touches nothing else; the taste tastes nothing else but the flavor of bread. Thus, the senses of the body are deceived; but the sense of the soul cannot be deceived, if the soul so wills—that is, if it does not wish to deprive itself of the light of most holy faith through infidelity <note>In this context, "infidelity" refers to a lack of belief or trust in the teachings of the Church.</note>. 

Who is it, then, that tastes and sees and touches this sacrament? It is the sense of the soul. With what eye does the soul see it? With the eye of the intellect, if the pupil of most holy faith is within it. This eye sees in that whiteness whole God and whole man: the divine nature joined with the human nature; the body, the soul, and the blood of <term>Christ<gloss>The original uses the Greek-derived abbreviation "xpo" (Christo).</gloss></term>; the soul united in the body, and the body and the soul united with my divine nature, never being separated from me. 

As you well remember, I manifested this to you in the beginning of your life. I showed it to you not only with the eye of the intellect, but even with the eye of your body—although, because of the great light, the eye of your body lost its power of sight, and only the sight of the eye of the intellect remained. And I showed this to you for your clarification, to protect you against the battle that the devil had given you concerning this very thing <note>Catherine frequently experienced visions that confirmed her faith when she was tempted by doubts or "spiritual battles" regarding the reality of the Eucharist.</note>. Wherefore you know: that going one morning at dawn to the church to hear the Mass, having been previously tormented by the devil...

# Providence 113

...cannot come in this life; and they are united in me. And I call them my Christs <note>original: "mei chriſti". A reference to the "anointed ones" (from the Latin *Christus*). In Catherine’s theology, priests are "other Christs" because they act in the person of Christ during the sacraments.</note>, because I have given them to administer me to you, and I have placed them like fragrant flowers in the mystical body of the <margin>just</margin> holy Church. This dignity the angel does not have, and I have given it to men—that is, to those whom I have elected as my ministers, whom I have placed as angels. They ought to be earthly angels in this life. Because they ought to be like angels, I require purity and charity in every soul, loving me and their neighbor, and helping them with what they have, then administering prayer to them while remaining in the delight of charity, just as in another place upon such matter I told you.

But much more greatly do I require purity in my ministers, and love toward me and their neighbor, as they administer the body and the blood of my only-begotten son with the fire of charity and with hunger for the salvation of souls, for the glory and praise of my name. And just as these ministers desire the cleanliness of the chalice where this sacrifice <note>The "sacrifice" refers to the Mass or the Consecration of the Host.</note> is made, so I seek the cleanliness and purity of the heart of the soul and of their mind, and the body as the instrument of the soul.

I want them to observe perfect purity, and I do not want them to nourish themselves or wallow in the mud of impurity, nor be swollen with pride, seeking great positions of authority <note>original: "prelatiōe". This refers to the rank of a prelate or high-ranking church official.</note>, nor be cruel toward themselves or toward their neighbor. For they cannot use their cruelty without their neighbor; because if they are cruel to themselves through <unclear>sin</unclear>, they are cruel to the souls of their neighbor, because they do not give them an example of a good life, nor do they care to pull souls from the hands of the demon, nor to administer to them the body and the blood of my only-begotten son—and me, the true light, as I have told you—nor the other sacraments of the holy Church. So it is that, being cruel to themselves, they are cruel to others.

### Of the Divine Chapter
<meta>catchword: doing</meta>

<image-desc>A woodcut decorative initial 'V' containing a portrait of a bearded saint (likely St. Catherine of Siena or a church father) in a habit, looking upwards towards a divine light or symbol in the upper left corner.</image-desc>

I also desire that my **ministers** <note>In this context, "ministers" refers specifically to priests and those ordained to serve the Church.</note> be generous and not avaricious: that is, that out of greed and **avarice** they do not sell my grace of the **Holy Spirit**. They must not, nor do I want them to do so: because just as they have received from my goodness out of the gift and abundance of **charity**, so out of a gift and with a heart open through the affection of love toward my honor and the salvation of souls, they ought to give charitably to every creature who possesses reason and who humbly asks for it. 

And they must not take anything for it <note>original: "p scio" likely meaning "prezzo" (price) or "per ciò" (for that).</note>, since they have not purchased it, but rather have received it by grace from me so that they might minister to you. However, they well can and should accept it as **alms**; and so the subject who receives should do, for he ought to give his portion when he can give it as an alms. For they [the ministers] ought to be fed by you with temporal things, assisting their necessity; and you ought to be fed and nourished by them with grace and spiritual gifts: that is, with the **holy sacraments** <term>Sacraments: the sacred rites of the Church, such as the Eucharist and Confession, believed to transmit divine grace.</term> that I have placed in the **Church**, because they minister them for your salvation. 

And I make it known to you that, beyond any comparison, they give more to you than you give to them. For no comparison can be made between finite and transitory things—such as the support provided to them—and me, God, who am infinite. By my **providence** and divine charity, I have placed them to minister to you. And this is not only true of this mystery <note>The "mystery" refers specifically to the Eucharist mentioned on the previous page.</note>, but of whatever thing it may be; and from whichever creature spiritual graces might be ministered to you through prayer or through any other thing, all your temporal **substances** <note>Material wealth, property, or goods.</note> combined would not equal, nor could they ever equal or correspond to that which you receive—especially without any comparison. 

Now I tell you: that the substance which they receive from you, they are bound to distribute in three ways: that is, to make of it three parts. One for their own life; the second to put into the church (that is, for things that are necessary); and the other for the poor. Otherwise, they act—

<summary>God explains that priests must provide spiritual graces and sacraments freely, as they received them freely, while the laity should provide for the priests' material needs through alms. He establishes a three-fold rule for how clergy should use their income: for their own needs, for the church, and for the poor.</summary>

### ¶ Of the dignity of priests: and how the virtue of the sacraments is not diminished by the sins of the ministers: and how God does not want secular people <note>In this context, "seculars" refers to the laity—those who are not ordained members of the clergy.</note> to interfere in correcting them. Chapter 115.

This is what those sweet and glorious ministers did, of whom I told you that I wanted you to see their excellence beyond the dignity I had given them—having made them "my Christs" <term>my Christs: from the Latin "Christos meos," meaning "my anointed ones," referring to the priestly role as an extension of Christ's own ministry</term>, as I told you. Those who exercise this dignity in virtue are clothed in this sweet and glorious Sun, which I gave to them to administer. Look upon sweet **Gregory**, **Sylvester**, and the other predecessors who followed the principal pontiff **Peter**, to whom the keys of the kingdom of heaven were given by my Life <note>A reference to Jesus Christ, whom the Father calls "my Truth" and "my Life."</note>. I said to Peter: "I give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven." <note>original: "io ti do le chiaue d'l regno del cielo: & cio che tu desliğerai in terra: sara desligato i cielo: & chi tu ligarai in tra: sera ligato i cielo." A direct translation of the mandate given to St. Peter in Matthew 16:19.</note>

Listen, dearest daughter: by manifesting to you the excellence of the virtues of these men, I will more fully show you the dignity in which I have placed these my ministers. This, then, is the key of the **Blood of my only-begotten Son**; this key opened **eternal life**, which for a long time had been locked by the **sin of Adam**. But once I gave you my Truth—that is, the Word of my only-begotten Son—He, by enduring death and passion, destroyed your death with His own death, making for you a bath of His blood. Thus the Blood and His death, by the power of my divine nature united with human nature, opened eternal life. To whom did He leave the keys of this Blood? To the glorious Apostle Peter and to all the others who have come and who will come from now until the last day of judgment. So it is that all have that same authority which Peter had; and no defect of theirs diminishes this authority, nor takes the perfection away from the Blood, nor from any sacrament. For I already told you that this Sun <note>The "Sun" is a recurring metaphor for the spiritual power of the sacraments; just as the sun's light can shine on filth without becoming dirty itself, the sacrament remains holy even if the priest is not.</note> could not be defiled by any filth.

<summary>God the Father explains to St. Catherine that the authority of the priesthood, inherited from St. Peter, is centered on the "key of the Blood." He emphasizes that the spiritual efficacy of the sacraments remains perfect and undefiled even if the minister performing them is sinful.</summary>

Of the Divine Chapter
<meta>catchword: three.</meta>

And the Sun does not lose its light because of the darkness of mortal sin that might be in the one who administers it, or in the one who receives it; for his guilt can do no harm to the sacraments of the Holy Church, nor diminish the virtue within them. However, sin does indeed diminish the grace and increase the guilt in the one who administers or receives them unworthily. 

So then, **Christ on earth** <note>"Christ on earth" (Italian: *Cristo in terra*) is Catherine’s habitual title for the Pope, indicating his role as the visible representative of Jesus.</note> holds the keys to the Blood, just as—if you remember well—I revealed to you in this image. Wishing to show you how much reverence the laity <note>original: "seculari," referring to those who are not ordained.</note> ought to have for these ministers, whether they be good or bad, and how much their [lack of] reverence displeased me, you know that I presented to you the mystical body of the Holy Church in the form of a **cellar** <term>cellar: original "telaro." In Catherine’s visions, the Church is often depicted as a wine cellar where the "wine" of Christ's Blood is stored to be dispensed by the Pope.</term>. 

In this cellar was the Blood of my only-begotten Son, and in that Blood all the sacraments have their value, and all have life by virtue of this Blood. At the door of this cellar was **Christ on earth**, to whom was committed the task of administering the Blood; and it was his responsibility to appoint ministers to help him administer it throughout the entire universal body of the Christian religion. 

Hence, whoever was accepted and anointed by him was made a minister, and no others. From him, therefore, has proceeded the entire clerical order; he has placed each one in his office to administer this glorious Blood. And just as he has appointed them as his helpers, it belongs only to him to correct their defects. This is how I wish it to be, because of the excellence and authority I have given them, having raised them up from "below"—that is, from the subjection and lordship of temporal rulers. 

So it is that civil law has nothing to do with their law or their punishment; that belongs only to the one who is appointed to rule over the divine law. These are my anointed ones, and therefore I said through the Scriptures: *Do not touch my Christs.* <note>original: "nō uogliate tochare li christi mei." A reference to Psalm 105:15. Here, "Christs" is used in the sense of "anointed ones."</note> Thus, a man can come to no greater ruin than by making himself their punisher.

# Providence CXVI

<margin>Chapter 116</margin>
Three. And if you were to ask me for what reason I showed you that the guilt of those who persecuted Holy Church was more grave than all other committed sins—given that I did not want the reverence toward my ministers to diminish because of their personal defects—I would answer you, and I do answer: it is because every act of reverence shown to them is actually shown to me, by virtue of the Blood that I have given them to administer. 

Otherwise, you would owe them no more reverence than you do to any other men of the world, and no more. You are constrained to show them reverence because of this ministry; for it is into their hands you must come—not for their own sake, but because of the power I have given them—if you wish to receive the holy sacraments of the Church. For if you are able to have these sacraments and yet refuse them, you would live and die in a state of damnation. 

Thus, the reverence is mine, and it belongs to this glorious Blood. We are one and the same thing through the union of the divine nature with the human nature <note>This refers to the "Hypostatic Union," the Christian doctrine that Jesus is both fully God and fully man.</note>, as has been said; the reverence is not for the men themselves. And just as the reverence is mine, so too is the injury. For I have already told you that you should not show reverence to them for their own persons, but for the authority I have given them. 

And for the same reason, they must not be offended; for by offending them, people offend me and not them. I have already forbidden it, and said: "I do not want my **Christs** to be touched by their hands." <note>original: "li mei christi." This is a reference to Psalm 105:15: "Touch not my anointed." In Catherine's theology, priests are "Christs" because they are anointed to act in the person of Christ.</note> 

Therefore, no one can excuse themselves by saying: "I am doing no injury, nor am I a rebel against Holy Church; I am only acting against the defects of wicked pastors." Such a person heaps judgment upon their own head. Blinded by self-love, they do not see—or rather, they see well enough, but pretend not to see so as to stifle the sting of their conscience. For they would see, and they do see, that they are persecuting the Blood and not the men. The injury is mine, just as the reverence was mine. And so every harm, mockery, insult, reproach, and dishonor... <note>The text cuts off here, likely continuing with "vituperio" (vituperation/dishonor) on the next page.</note>

...by their own malice and with deliberation; and they know that they cannot do these things with a good **conscience**, yet by doing them they offend. The soul is consumed because it is deprived of **grace**, and often the **worm of conscience** <note>A common medieval metaphor for the persistent, gnawing guilt that torments a sinner's mind.</note> gnaws at them; their temporal substance is consumed in the service of the devil, and their bodies die like animals. So then, this **sin** is committed properly against me, and it is done without any color of personal utility or any delight, but only with malice and with the smoke of pride. This pride is born from self-centered sensory love and from that perverse fear that **Pilate** <note>Referring to Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to death. Catherine often uses him as an example of those who do evil to protect their worldly status.</note> had, who, for fear of losing his dominion, killed Christ my only-begotten son. This is how these people have acted and continue to act.

All other sins are committed either through simplicity, or through ignorance of not knowing, or through **malice**—that is, the person knows well the evil he does, but because of the disordered delight and pleasure he has in that sin, or because of some utility he might find in it, he offends. And by offending, he does harm; he offends his own soul, and me, and his neighbor. He offends me because he does not give glory and praise to my name. And he offends his neighbor because he does not offer him the affection of my **charity**; though he does not strike me "actually"—that is, in a way that is directed properly at me—he offends himself, and this offense displeases me because of the harm it does to him. 

But this aforementioned offense <note>The persecution of the clergy.</note> is an offense committed against my very self without any intermediary. Other sins have some "color" <note>original: "colore". In this context, it means a pretext, excuse, or outward appearance of a reason.</note> and are committed with a pretext, and they are committed through an intermediary. By offending the neighbor, then, they offend me through them. ### ¶ A summary regarding the aforementioned things about the Holy Church and its ministers. Chapter 118.

And because the mystery of the **Sacrament** <note>original: "scrō", abbreviation for "sacramento"</note> cannot be diminished or divided by their defects, the reverence toward them should never fail—not for their own sake, as has been said, but for the treasure of the **Blood**. 

In doing the contrary, I have shown you a small thing (in respect to its actual gravity) regarding how serious and displeasing it is to me, and how damaging it is to them: this irreverence and persecution of the **Blood**, and the bond formed against me which they have made together, bound in the service of the devil. And I have told you this so that you may grieve more deeply. This is one defect which I have described to you particularly regarding the persecution of the **Holy Church**; and I tell you the same generally regarding the Christian religion: those who live in **mortal sin** <note>original: "pctō mortale"</note> and despise the **Blood**, depriving themselves of the life of **grace**. This, then, displeases me, and very grave is the guilt of those I have specifically described to you, just as has been said.

Also with this light, I want you to know the darkness and the matter of my ministers, of whom I told you I would speak. 

Open then the eye of your intellect and look at me, the **Sun of Justice** <note>original: "sole de iustitia," a traditional title for God emphasizing his role as the source of all truth and rightness</note>, and you will see the glorious ministers who, having administered the Sun, have taken on the condition of the Sun—as I told you. **Peter** is the chief of the **Apostles**, who received the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and I tell you the same of others, who in this garden of the **Holy Church** have administered the light: that is, the body and the blood of my only-begotten Son, a sun joined and not divided, as has been said; and all the **Sacraments** of the Holy Church, which all give life by virtue of the **Blood**. 

Everyone is placed in a different rank according to their state to minister the grace of the **Holy Spirit**. As they have administered it with the light of grace, and which they have drawn from this true light: this light is single; no, because the light of **grace** <note>original: "grā"</note> cannot be alone, nor can it be divided. 

Whoever stays in **mortal sin** <note>original: "pcto mortale"</note> is immediately deprived of the light of grace; and whoever has grace is enlightened by the eye of their intellect to know me, who have given them grace, and the virtue that preserves grace. And they know in that light the misery of sin and the cause of sin—that is, selfish sensory love—and therefore they hate it. And hating it, they receive the heat of divine **charity** in their affection <note>In Catherine’s theology, "affection" refers to the faculty of the Will.</note>, because affection follows the intellect; and they receive the color of this glorious light, following the doctrine of my sweet **Truth** <note>Catherine often uses "Truth" as a personal name for Christ.</note>, whereby their memory is filled with the remembrance of the benefit of the **Blood**. 

So you see: they cannot receive the light without receiving the heat and the color, because they are united together and are one and the same thing. And so they cannot, as I told you, have one **power of the soul** <note>The three "powers of the soul" are Memory, Intellect, and Will; Catherine teaches they must be unified to reach God.</note> ordered to receive me, the true Sun, without all three being ordered and gathered in my name: because as soon as the eye of the intellect, with the light of faith, rises above sensory sight...

### Providence CXIX

By contemplating themselves in me: the affection <note>original: "laffecto," referring to the faculty of the soul's will or capacity to love</note> follows after it, loving that which the eye of the intellect saw and knew. And the memory fills itself with that which the affection loves. Thus you see that they have taken on the condition of the sun: that is, being clothed and having their faculties filled by me, the true Sun—as I have told you. 

They are like the sun, for the sun warms and illuminates, and with its heat it makes the earth germinate. Just so, these sweet ministers of mine—chosen, anointed, and placed in the <term>mystical body</term> <note>original: "corpo mistico," a theological term for the collective community of the Church</note> of the **Holy Church** to administer me, the Sun (that is, the body and the blood of my only-begotten Son and the other **Sacraments** which have life from this **Blood**) actually and mentally administer it. That is to say, they provide light within the mystical body of the Holy Church. 

By light, I mean the light of supernatural knowledge, along with the color of an honest and holy life: that is, following the doctrine of my Truth. They also administer the heat of most burning **charity**. Therefore, with their heat, they made sterile souls sprout, illuminating them with the light of knowledge; and with their holy and orderly lives, they drove away the darkness of **mortal sins** and of much infidelity. They brought order to the lives of those who were living in a disordered way in the darkness of sin and in the coldness caused by the deprivation of charity. 

So you see, then, that they are "suns," because they have taken on the condition of the sun from me, the true Sun. Through the affection of love, they are made one thing with me, and I with them—just as I have told you in another place. And to everyone I have given according to their state. # Of the Divine Chapter
### Page XIX

[hearts were] not bound in one and the same body: that is, under one and the same shepherd. But if he is a true and good physician of those souls—as were those glorious shepherds of old—he will not apply ointment without the fire of reproof <note>original: "reprehensione," referring to the necessity of firm correction alongside mercy</note>. And if the member <note>In this context, a "member" refers to an individual person within the communal "body" of the Church</note> should still be obstinate in his wrongdoing, he will cut him off from the congregation so that he does not rot the rest with the stench of <term>mortal sin</term> <note>original: "peccato mortale," the most serious category of sins which are believed to destroy divine grace within the soul</note>; but they do not do this; rather, they pretend not to see. And do you know why? Because the root of <term>self-love</term> <note>original: "amore proprio," a central theme in Catherine’s work, describing the selfish ego that replaces love for God</note> lives in them, from which they draw a perverse <term>servile fear</term> <note>original: "timore seruile," a fear motivated by the threat of personal loss or punishment rather than a "holy fear" motivated by love</note>. Out of fear of losing their position, or temporal things, or their high office, they do not correct; nor do they recognize in what way their position is truly preserved. For if they saw justice, they would maintain it; but because they are deprived of light, they do not know it.

Wherefore, believing they preserve their status through injustice—by not rebuking the faults of those under them—they are deceived by their own sensual passions and by the hunger for power or high office. They also do not correct because they themselves are guilty of those same faults, or even greater ones. Therefore, feeling themselves caught in the same guilt, they lose their courage and confidence; and bound by servile fear, they pretend not to see. And even if they do see, they do not correct, but allow themselves to be bound by flattering words and by many gifts; wherefore they themselves find excuses not to punish. In these men is fulfilled the word which <term>my Truth</term> <note>Catherine uses "my Truth" as a title for Jesus Christ, who is speaking through her</note> spoke in the holy Gospel, saying: "These are blind, and leaders of the blind; and if one blind man leads another, both fall into the ditch" <note>A translation of the reference to Matthew 15:14: "Caeci sunt, et duces caecorum..."</note>.

Those who have been my sweet ministers—of whom I told you that they had the nature and quality of the sun—did not and do not act this way. And truly they are suns, as I have told you: for in them there is no darkness of sin, nor ignorance, because they follow the doctrine of my Truth. They are despisers of greatness, of high status, and of the delights of the world; and therefore they do not fear to correct.
